events.title: The death of Pope Gelasius II at Cluny
events.shortBlurb: Hunted from Rome by the emperor's faction, Pope Gelasius II died in exile at Cluny after a pontificate of a single year…
body: John of Gaeta, a monk of Monte Cassino, had been made cardinal in 1088 and chancellor in 1089 by Urban II, and had served Paschal II in the same office. On 24 January 1118 the cardinals chose him pope as Gelasius II — and that very night the Frangipani, the emperor's allies in Rome, seized and maltreated him until the people broke in and set him free.

He fled to Gaeta, where he was ordained priest and consecrated bishop in March, while Henry V set up the excommunicated archbishop of Braga as the antipope Gregory VIII. From Capua that April Gelasius excommunicated the emperor and his creature, and when Rome could no longer hold him he sailed by Pisa into France.

He reached the abbey of Cluny and died there on 29 January 1119, having suffered more in one year, his contemporaries said, than any pope since the age of the martyrs. The cardinals with him chose Callixtus II in the same abbey on 2 February, and three years later the Concordat of Worms brought the long struggle over investiture towards its end.
